summary: HTTP/3 connection migration causing duplicate rate-accounting and intermittent 429s during concurrent multipart uploads
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using Cordis client library on dedicated pool report intermittent 429s during large parallel multipart uploads over HTTP/3. Failures appear as soft 429s (burst/accounting) rather than hard quota exhaustion.

Impact:
- Several background and interactive upload workers received 429s for short windows (~5-20s) affecting downstream ingestion pipelines.
- Customer seeing increased error rate, delayed ingest completion, and retries causing higher cost.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-07), prod, us-west-2.
- Client: Cordis analytics platform, custom uploader using HTTP/3 (QUIC) with concurrent file chunks (8-16 parallel streams).

Steps to reproduce (observed / customer repro):
1) Start large multipart ingest with 12 parallel chunk uploads using HTTP/3 from a single host behind NAT.
2) After ~30–90s, client triggers connection migration (mobile host sleeps/wakes, or local network switch).
3) Incoming requests succeed briefly, then a spike of 429 responses logged by the client for multiple concurrent chunk requests.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include our throttle reason header: X-Rate-Limit-Reason: burst_accounting.
- Server ingress logs show duplicate token-charge entries for the same logical upload sequence_id when connection migration occurs (different connection IDs, same upload metadata).
- Error windows are short and recover when upload retries with backoff.

Expected behavior:
- Connection migration should not double-charge the tenant route token buckets for the same logical session/upload. Uploads should continue or be gracefully rate-limited according to configured burst pools without duplicate accounting.

Quick logs (redacted):
- 2026-03-12T08:12:03Z ingress-edge-01 req_id=uvq9f chunk_id=alpha conn_id=0x7a3a status=200 charges=1
- 2026-03-12T08:12:13Z ingress-edge-01 req_id=uvq9f chunk_id=alpha conn_id=0x9f2b status=200 charges=1  <-- same req_id but new conn_id after migration
- 2026-03-12T08:12:14Z rate-limiter req_id=uvq9f tenant=cordis charges_applied=2 window=1s result=throttle
- 2026-03-12T08:12:15Z client CordisUploader error=429 upload_seq=12345 chunk=alpha
investigation_notes: 03/12 09:00 - Reproduced locally using Cordis test harness with HTTP/3 and simulated connection migration (netem bring-down/up). Observed duplicate accounting when migration occurred mid-upload.

03/12 10:15 - Hypothesis: ingress-proxy attaches token-accounting keyed by (connection_id, route_key). When QUIC connection migration occurs, a new connection_id is created but request metadata (upload seq, route) remains the same, causing a second charge for the same logical unit.

03/12 11:30 - Rate-limiter pipeline uses short-lived per-connection dedupe caches but TTL is too short to catch migration window; cache miss leads to double charge. Cache hit rate around migration is 0%.
03/12 12:00 - Edge-telemetry shows NAT IP reuse and connection-id churn correlate with 429 spikes for this customer (highly concurrent chunking).
03/13 09:45 - Confirmed non-HTTP/3 clients (HTTP/1.1 over TLS) do not trigger the same double-count behavior under similar migration tests.
03/13 14:00 - Temporary mitigation tested: increase per-connection dedupe TTL to 10s reduced duplicate charges but had memory pressure on edge proxies during mass parallel uploads.
comments: Maya Chen (Mar 12 09:20): Customer reported bursty 429s after switching uploader to HTTP/3. Provided logs and timeline. Asked for escalation to edge team.
Liam O'Riley (Mar 12 09:45): Acknowledged. Reproducing locally. Tentatively tagging ingress-proxy and rate-limiter. Assigned INT-4421 to track infra follow-up.
EdgeEngBot (Mar 12 11:10): Attached pcap and QUIC trace to GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/issues/2239 (internal).
Cordis Support (Mar 12 12:05): Confirmed repro steps and approved short-term instrumentation changes for their dedicated pool.

Liam O'Riley (Mar 13 15:30): Deployed config change to increase dedupe TTL to 10s on canary edge nodes in us-west-2. Observed reduced duplicate charging but memory OOM risk on heavy concurrent tenants.
next_steps: (Short term) Rollback TTL increase to safe level on non-dedicated nodes; keep elevated TTL only for customer-dedicated-07 traffic via route tag (canary).
(Short term) Provide Cordis with client-side workaround: disable QUIC connection migration or implement robust idempotency-key per-chunk that the edge will honor across connection migration.
(Medium term) Implement idempotent accounting key: prefer (tenant, route, upload_seq, chunk_id) dedupe in rate-limiter upstream of per-connection key so migration does not double-charge.
(Medium term) Add safe eviction policy and bounded memory for dedupe cache to handle bursty parallel uploads without OOM.
(Long term) Update docs: Guidance for high-concurrency multipart uploads over HTTP/3 and recommended client idempotency headers.
resolution_notes: Workarounds provided to Cordis: 1) disable HTTP/3 connection migration in their uploader (immediate); 2) add idempotency-key per chunk to avoid duplicate accounting across reconnects. Engineering implemented a targeted canary with increased dedupe TTL for route 'customer-dedicated-07' which reduced 429 windows. Follow-up ticket INT-4421 opened to implement robust dedupe by logical upload key and bounded cache with eviction policy. No user data corruption observed; issue root cause: per-connection accounting semantics with QUIC migration.
